title: fix(plugin-dashboard): make a metric tile say which measures it drops
body:
Part of #8894 — the **(b)** half only, per the PM verdict on that card (comment 5608893821): make the drop **speak**, do not render it.

⚠️ **This deliberately leaves the card open.** #8894 also carries **(a)** — rendering `values[1..]` as secondary tile values — which gives those entries authoring semantics they do not have today, i.e. a widening on the manual-floor route. That half stays open there, and it is the one expected to flip the pins named below. That is also why this PR says `Part of` and keeps every issue-closing keyword away from an issue number.

## What changed

`values` is `z.array(z.string()).min(1)` on `DashboardWidgetSchema`, so declaring three measures on a metric-family widget has always been legal; `DatasetWidget` sends every one of them to the server (`measures: values`) and its metric branch then renders `values[0]` and stops. It did that in complete silence — no warning, no console message, no visual tell. A tile answering a narrower question than its metadata asked reads as a finished product, and **that silence is the defect** (ADR-0049 declared-but-unenforced), not the two numbers that never appeared.

One `useEffect` in `DatasetWidget` now emits a single `console.warn` naming the widget, its dataset, the measure that won, and each measure that did not. This is the same shape `warnSuppressedListNav` (ADR-0047, objectui#2338) already uses in this monorepo for a suppressed list-view control.

**Nothing renders differently.** The tile's markup is byte-for-byte what it was; the measures after the first are still dropped.

### The wording is load-bearing

The message says the dropped measures are **queried and then never displayed** — never that they are "ignored" or "unused", and a test pins that it does not say so. P2 below is why: they are not inert, and a message claiming they were would be a second false statement layered on the first.

### Shape chosen: warn, not refuse

Stating it explicitly because the verdict asked for it: **this is not a refusal and not a narrowing of the accept set.** No document that stores today stops storing, no widget that renders today stops rendering, and no parse that succeeds today starts failing. The only new thing in the world is a console line.

## P1 and P2, measured before any code was written

**P1 — a metric-family widget declaring more than one measure is rare. TRUE.** Census enumerated from `git ls-files` (so the enumeration and the reads share one source), classifying by the renderer's own rule `METRIC_TYPES.has(type) || dimensions.length === 0`:

| population | metric-family, `values.length === 1` (positive control) | metric-family, `values.length > 1` (subject) |
|---|---|---|
| this repo | **176** | 9 raw hits |
| `objectstack` | **168** | 5 raw hits |

⭐ The positive control lights up in both trees, so the small number is a reading and not a broken probe. Every one of the 14 raw multi-measure hits was then read individually, and **not one is a dashboard metric tile**: 13 are `ReportSchema` shapes (`type: summary` / `matrix`, which route to `DatasetReportRenderer`, never to this component, and my classifier only called them metric-family because they carry no `dimensions` key) plus one `bar` chart-binding test. The 14th is **PR #8887's own reproduction case** in this repo — the duly#109 tile. So the authored population of the shape this warns about is **zero**, in both trees, and a warn cannot flood anything.

**P2 — the extra measures are inert. FALSE AS STATED, and the message is worded around it.** They are genuinely never *displayed*: on the metric branch there is no export, no drill-down, no tooltip and no `compareTo` path that reads past `values[0]` (`comparedValues` is computed over all of them but only consulted for `values[0]`), and the metric loading skeleton does not size itself from the measure count. But three live reads of `values[1..]` remain:

1. `measures: values` — the server computes every one of them (this is the card's own claim, re-verified);
2. they join the widget's refetch `signature`, so editing them refetches;
3. `options.sortBy` is accepted when `values.includes(sortBy)` — so a *second* declared measure legalizes a `sortBy` that would otherwise degrade to unordered. On a `metric`-**typed** widget that also declares dimensions (`isMetric` is true by type, so it keeps tile shape while the query returns many rows), that decides which row becomes `rows[0]` and therefore **which number the tile shows**.

⇒ "declared but not rendered" is true; "declared but useless" is not. The message claims only the first, and a test asserts it does not claim the second.

## The two controls from PR #8887 — both untouched, both green

1. **The byte-isomorphism control** (`BASELINE_NO_SUBCAPTION` in `DatasetWidget.subCaption.test.tsx`) — a tile declaring no sub-caption must render identical bytes. A console-level signal never reaches the DOM, so this was never at risk. Green.
2. ⭐⭐ **The "those measures are still dropped" pin** (`expect(container.textContent).not.toContain('7')` / `not.toContain('3')`) — the strongest out-of-bounds self-check on this card. Going (b) does not change that fact, so **that pin did not move**: `DatasetWidget.subCaption.test.tsx` is not in this PR's file list at all. Green.

This PR adds its own control on the same axis, from this card's side: the three-measure tile's `innerHTML` is asserted byte-for-byte to be one number and one caption. If it ever goes red, the change grew (a)'s rendering semantics and owes the manual floor.

## Tests

New file `DatasetWidget.unrenderedMeasures-8894.test.tsx`, 8 cases, split explicitly into subjects and controls because a control that passes for a subject is how a change ships untested. Each `SUBJECT` asserts something **false before this change** — there was no warning at all to assert about:

- names both dropped measures, and does **not** call them ignored/unused/no-effect;
- identifies the widget, its dataset and the measure that won;
- speaks about the declaration, so a failed query does not mute it;
- covers the dimensionless arm (`type: bar` with no dimensions is a tile too);
- covers the `metric`-typed-with-dimensions arm.

Each `CONTROL` is green on **both** sides of the change: a single-measure tile stays silent; a real chart that renders all three measures stays silent; the markup is unchanged.

Evidence, every run below re-executed on the final commit `96e8e8a20` after the last edit, under this container's shared heavy-verify lock (`VERDICT command-exit 0 · held the lock 188s`):

- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-dashboard type-check` → exit 0. It earned its keep: on the first pass it caught two real `TS7006` implicit-`any` parameters in the new test file, which the vitest run had been perfectly happy with.
- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/plugin-dashboard/` → `Test Files 102 passed (102) · Tests 910 passed (910)`. This subsumes both the new file and `DatasetWidget.subCaption.test.tsx`.
- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/sdui-parser/src/__tests__/dashboard-widget-options-census.test.ts` → `Tests 12 passed (12)`. That census extracts the CONSUMED option set from `DatasetWidget.tsx`'s **source text** and is documented to fail loudly when that file moves underneath it, so it is on the content axis for any edit to this file — including one that only adds comments mentioning `options.sortBy`.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-dashboard lint` → exit 0, `450 problems (0 errors, 450 warnings)` — all pre-existing `no-explicit-any` warnings, none in the changed lines.
- `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` → exit 0, `1 source file(s) of 1 released package(s) changed, and this change declares 1 changeset(s)`.
- `node scripts/check-control-bytes.mjs` → exit 0, `scanned 7087 tracked text file(s)`; plus a direct `grep -naP` over the three changed files, no hits.
- `node scripts/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test` → `NOT GOVERNED — 3 path(s) checked against 5 governed surface(s); none matched`.

**Ablation**, from the committed tree at `96e8e8a20`: the `console.warn` call was replaced with a `void` of the same expression. The mutation was proven to reach disk *before* anything ran — marker `console.warn(unrenderedMeasureWarning)` 1 to 0, replacement marker 0 to 1, and `git hash-object` moving from the `HEAD` blob `bd545ca9…` to `6a505257…`. Result: **exactly the 5 `SUBJECT` cases went red, by name**, all 3 `CONTROL` cases stayed green, and `DatasetWidget.subCaption.test.tsx` stayed green throughout (`Tests 5 failed | 15 passed (20)`). The tree was then restored **by state** — `git hash-object` back to `bd545ca9…` **and** `git diff HEAD` empty — never by an exit code. The mutating script carries `trap ... EXIT INT TERM` with absolute paths. No `dist/` is involved: the root `vitest.config.mts` aliases every `@object-ui/*` specifier to that package's `src/` and the test imports `../DatasetWidget` relatively, so the ablation reads source directly.

## Line-number citations (position axis)

Enumerated from `git ls-files`, splitting citations into **stored** (inside code, so they can be keyed or compared, and go stale mechanically) and **prose** (inside comments or markdown, printed for a reader and never compared). Run on all three carriers the strong form asks for — `origin/main`, this branch, and the tree produced by a real `git merge --no-ff` of this branch into `origin/main` in a one-off detached worktree — and all three agree:

- **stored literals citing the changed files: 0.** Nothing keys on a line number in `DatasetWidget.tsx`; the ledger that does key on `path:line` (`UNGATED_EXAMPLES` in `scripts/check-doc-example-types.mjs`) carries no `plugin-dashboard` row.
- **prose citations: 7** (in `data-objectstack`, `types`, `i18n` and this package). This PR shifts lines below the insertion point, so those go stale as documentation. They are objectui#8875's lane and are **not touched** here; `CHANGELOG.md` line numbers are never touched at all.

## Clause-②

**`Clause-②: yes`**, declared on both carriers.

The mechanical floor does not force it: this diff adds no exported symbol, no schema key, no new member of any enum or union, no registry entry and no new key on any published payload, and it neither widens nor narrows the accept set. It is judged `yes` on the honest-uncertainty rule instead, for a reason worth a reviewer's minute: a new runtime diagnostic that fires on **currently legal** authored metadata is a normative statement about the authoring contract — "declaring this is a mistake" — and that statement is exactly what (a) would overturn. Better to have it read than to assume it.

## 验收备注

- **objectui#8894 stays open** and now carries only (a). The successor there is the one that renders `values[1..]`, and it is expected to flip both of #8887's pins and the DOM control added here.
- **This does not answer `objectstack-ai/duly` #109.** That card wants the *numbers*, which is (a). Its documented workaround — declaring only `approved_rate` and saying so in the module header — is unchanged by this PR. What changes is that the next author who reaches for three measures is told, instead of being quietly given one.
- **Noted, not filed — the `options.sortBy` reach described under P2.** A second declared measure legalizing a `sortBy` whose only effect is to pick which row a tile reads is a surprising amount of leverage for a declaration the tile does not otherwise honour. It is not a defect against any stated contract, no authored widget in either tree does it, and naming it inside this PR would have required either widening the message past what it can prove or touching the query path. Successor: the (a) card on objectui#8894, which has to decide what `values[1..]` mean anyway.
- **Noted, not filed — the designer says nothing either.** `WidgetConfigPanel` lets an author add a second measure to a metric widget with no signal at all; this PR speaks only at render. The PM verdict named an authoring-time signal as the alternative shape had P1 come back false. P1 came back true, so the cheap half shipped. Successor: whoever takes the (a) card, since a designer that warns about a shape (a) is about to make legal would be wrong the day it lands.
